checks.s: The document identifies the Sponsor as BioNovara Therapeutics, Inc. and states that it is a Delaware corporation.
The document states the Sponsor's principal office address as 900 Innovation Parkway, Suite 400, Cambridge, MA 02142.
The document states the Sponsor's EIN as 84-3921057.
The document states the Sponsor's FEI as 3019847562.
The document identifies the CMO as Pinnacle Sterile Manufacturing, LLC and states that it is an Indiana LLC.
The document states the CMO's principal office address as 7200 Lakeshore Industrial Boulevard, Bloomington, IN 47404.
The document states the CMO's EIN as 35-6847293.
The document states the CMO's FEI as 3007261948.
The document identifies the product as LANREVA® (lanrecotide acetate injection, 50 mg/mL).
The document states that the dosage form is a pre-filled syringe with a 1.0 mL fill volume.
The document states that the route of administration is subcutaneous.
The document references NDA #216-487 and an approval date of January 22, 2024.
The document states a 24-month shelf life at 2–8 °C.
The document references DMF #035812 held by Pinnacle for its aseptic fill-finish process and facility.
The document references DMF #031476 held by Kessler AG for the lanrecotide acetate drug substance.
The document states that the CMO performs QC testing and issues the Certificate of Analysis (CoA) and Certificate of Compliance (CoC).

The document states that the Sponsor's QA independently reviews batch records, CoA, CoC, deviation reports, and environmental monitoring data, and issues final product release for commercial distribution.
The document explicitly states that the Sponsor retains final authority over batch disposition, referencing 21 CFR 211.22 or equivalent language.
The document assigns Phase I (laboratory) and Phase II (manufacturing) OOS investigations to the CMO.
The document reserves to the Sponsor oversight and approval authority before any reprocessing or batch disposition decision.
The document prohibits the CMO from unilaterally closing an OOS investigation or approving reprocessing without Sponsor approval.
The document classifies Minor changes as Annual Reportable and allows CMO implementation after Sponsor written acknowledgment within a 10 business-day review period.
The document classifies Moderate changes as CBE-30, requires Sponsor approval before implementation, and requires 90 calendar days' advance notice from the CMO.
The document classifies Major changes as PAS, requires Sponsor approval with minimum 12 months' advance notice, and requires CMO cooperation with any required FDA supplement.
The document requires the CMO to obtain the Sponsor's prior written approval for any GMP-relevant change.
The document explicitly includes supplier changes for critical components from Arvida Glass and/or Helios Elastomer within the scope of the change control provisions.
The document provides the Sponsor with up to 2 scheduled audits per calendar year, each up to 5 business days.
The document provides the Sponsor with unlimited for-cause audits upon 48 hours' notice.
The document requires the CMO to prepare the draft Annual Product Quality Review within 60 calendar days after each calendar year-end.
The document requires the Sponsor to review and finalize the APQR within 30 calendar days after receipt of the CMO draft.

The document states that, when a batch failure is due to CMO manufacturing error, the CMO bears the cost of API replacement at the Sponsor's API transfer price of $3,420 per batch (2.1 kg × $1,628.57/kg) plus re-manufacture at no charge, consistent with MSA § 7.3.
The document states that the Sponsor bears all costs when a batch failure is due to Sponsor-supplied API non-conformance.
The document states that disputed root cause triggers a joint investigation and that unresolved disputes are escalated to Hargrove Compliance Advisors, LLC within 45 calendar days.
The document states that the Sponsor makes all recall decisions exclusively.
The document states that the CMO must cooperate in recalls and bears full costs when a recall is attributable to the CMO's manufacturing or testing failures.
The document states that recall costs for joint or indeterminate causation are shared 60% Sponsor / 40% CMO, consistent with MSA § 9.4.
Exhibit C or an equivalent key personnel section lists Dr. Priya Ramanathan, SVP Quality Assurance, BioNovara as Sponsor QA signatory or head of Quality Unit.
Exhibit C or an equivalent key personnel section lists Laura Chen-Whitfield, VP Regulatory Affairs, BioNovara as Sponsor regulatory affairs contact.
Exhibit C or an equivalent key personnel section lists Michael Trent Ostrowski, VP Quality Operations, Pinnacle as CMO QA signatory or head of CMO Quality Unit.
Exhibit C or an equivalent key personnel section lists Sarah Nakamura-Davis, Director Site Quality Assurance, Pinnacle as CMO day-to-day quality contact.
The document names Hargrove Compliance Advisors, LLC (Raleigh, NC) as the agreed independent cGMP expert for disputed root-cause investigations.
The document includes the escalation ladder in this order: Joint Quality Council → Independent cGMP Expert (Hargrove) → MSA arbitration clause.
The governing law section specifies the State of Delaware.
The dispute resolution section references binding arbitration under JAMS rules seated in New York, NY, consistent with MSA § 14.
The document routes technical/scientific quality disputes through the Joint Quality Council and Independent cGMP Expert before MSA arbitration.
The document references CMO minimum product liability coverage of $25,000,000 per occurrence / $50,000,000 aggregate, per MSA § 12.1.
The document references Sponsor minimum product liability coverage of $50,000,000 per occurrence / $100,000,000 aggregate, per MSA § 12.1.
Exhibit A includes an assay specification of 98.0–102.0% label claim by HPLC.
Exhibit A specifies related substances limits of individual impurity NMT 0.5% and total NMT 2.0%.
Exhibit A includes a pH specification of 4.0–5.0.
Exhibit A includes sterility testing per USP <71>.
Exhibit A specifies bacterial endotoxins NMT 5.0 EU/mL per USP <85>.
Exhibit A includes container closure integrity per USP <1207>.
Exhibit A specifies a fill volume of 1.00 ± 0.05 mL.
Exhibit A includes particulate matter testing per USP <788>.
Exhibit A includes syringe functionality tests per ISO 11040-4 or equivalent.
Exhibit A includes an appearance test.
Exhibit D lists Arvida Glass Technologies, S.r.l. (Padova, Italy) for Type I borosilicate glass pre-filled syringe barrels (Ompi EZ-Fill® format, 1.0 mL long, with staked needle).
Exhibit D lists Helios Elastomer Solutions GmbH (Mannheim, Germany) for elastomeric plunger stoppers (bromobutyl rubber, FluroTec® coated).
Exhibit D identifies the CMO as the procuring party for these critical components per Sponsor-approved specifications.

Exhibit B contains a RACI-style or comparable responsibility matrix covering cGMP obligations under 21 CFR Parts 210, 211, and 4 and ICH Q7/Q10, with responsibilities clearly allocated between Sponsor and CMO.

Exhibit B's matrix covers all 18 required areas: incoming material testing and release, in-process controls, finished product QC testing, batch record review, batch disposition/release, environmental monitoring, stability program, change control, deviation/CAPA management, OOS investigations, APQR, complaint handling, recall execution, regulatory inspection hosting, supplier qualification, training, document retention, and pharmacovigilance.
The document states that the drug substance (lanrecotide acetate API) is Sponsor-supplied and manufactured by Kessler AG (Basel, Switzerland).
The document states that primary packaging components (glass barrels and plunger stoppers) are CMO-procured from Sponsor-approved suppliers per Sponsor-approved specifications.
The document addresses incoming API testing and release by the CMO upon receipt.
The document requires the CMO to promptly notify the Sponsor of any FDA or other regulatory inspection of the manufacturing site.
The document provides the Sponsor the right to participate in or be represented during inspections related to the product.
The document requires the CMO to share inspection observations (e.g., FDA Form 483) and proposed responses with the Sponsor for review before submission.
The document describes the CMO facility as having an ISO Class 5 (Grade A) isolator-based filling environment on Line 3 within an ISO Class 7 (Grade B) background.
The document references the CMO's current EU GMP Certificate IT/2024/GMP/00487, issued by AIFA and valid through June 4, 2027.
The document references the CMO's FDA inspection of August 12–23, 2024 with an NAI outcome.
The document requires the CMO to notify the Sponsor within defined timelines of product quality complaints that may involve adverse events.
The document identifies the Sponsor, as NDA holder, as responsible for pharmacovigilance and regulatory filings.
The document states that the Quality Agreement's effective date is March 14, 2025 and its initial term runs through March 13, 2030, aligned with or co-extensive with the MSA.
The document includes two 2-year renewal options, with the latest expiration on March 13, 2034, aligned with the MSA.
The document requires amendment by mutual written agreement of both parties' Quality heads or equivalent senior quality officials.
The signature block designates Dr. Priya Ramanathan, SVP Quality Assurance, BioNovara Therapeutics, Inc. as the Sponsor signatory and includes lines for signature, printed name, title, and date.

The signature block designates Michael Trent Ostrowski, VP Quality Operations, Pinnacle Sterile Manufacturing, LLC as the CMO signatory and includes lines for signature, printed name, title, and date.
The document explicitly states that, in the event of a conflict between the Quality Agreement and the MSA, the Quality Agreement controls with respect to cGMP and quality-related matters.
The document explicitly states that, in the event of a conflict, the MSA controls with respect to purely commercial matters.
The recitals or introductory sections reference 21 CFR Parts 210, 211, and 4.
The recitals or introductory sections reference ICH Q7 and ICH Q10.
The recitals or introductory sections reference the FDA Guidance for Industry on Contract Manufacturing Arrangements for Drugs: Quality Agreements (September 2016).

Exhibit E is populated with the three-tier change control classification system using the negotiated timelines—Minor: 10 business-day review; Moderate: 90 calendar days' advance notice; Major: 12 months' advance notice—and these match the instruction email values, not template defaults.
Exhibit A (Product Description and Specifications) is present and populated with deal-specific LANREVA® product specifications, not left as a placeholder.
Exhibit B (Responsibility Matrix) is present and populated with deal-specific RACI allocations, not left as a placeholder.
Exhibit C (Key Personnel and Contact List) is present and populated with named individuals, not left as a placeholder.
Exhibit D (Approved Suppliers of Critical Components) is present and populated with specific supplier names and materials, not left as a placeholder.
Exhibit E (Change Control Classification and Notification Timelines) is present and populated with the three-tier system and timelines, not left as a placeholder.
Exhibit F (Batch Disposition and Release Workflow) is present and populated with the dual-release workflow, not left as a placeholder.
The document specifies that the CMO performs stability storage at 2–8 °C and testing per the approved protocol.
The document specifies that the Sponsor reviews stability data and makes decisions regarding shelf-life extensions or changes.

The Quality Agreement body does not include unit pricing ($14.85/PFS), payment terms, or other purely commercial terms, and commercial figures appear only as cross-references to specific MSA sections.
The Quality Agreement cross-references MSA § 7.3 for batch liability, MSA § 9.4 for recall cost-sharing, and MSA § 12.1 for insurance in the relevant cost allocation provisions.
